app.title: DSO3D12 Viewer
app.no_capture_loaded: No capture loaded — use Load Capture…
label.deleted: Deleted capture #%{n}. Press Undo to restore.
label.standard_fw_1: 1. Connect the oscilloscope to the computer using a USB Type-C cable.
label.standard_fw_2: 2. Feed a signal into the oscilloscope.
label.standard_fw_3: 3. Press Stop to freeze the sample buffer.
label.standard_fw_4: 4. Press Menu → Stop and leave the Channel 1 Measurements menu open.
label.standard_fw_5: 5. In the application, select the serial port and click Listen.
label.standard_fw_6: 6. Long-press the Save button on the oscilloscope to start transmitting the debug data.
label.standard_fw_7: 7. Wait for the transfer to complete. The oscilloscope sends approximately 300 kB at 115200 baud.
label.customized_fw_1: 1. Connect the oscilloscope to the computer using a USB Type-C cable.
label.customized_fw_2: 2. In the application, select the serial port and click Listen.
label.customized_fw_3: 3. Capture a waveform on the oscilloscope by pressing Save while acquisition is running or stopped.
label.customized_fw_4: 4. Press Menu → Gallery to open the saved screenshots.
label.customized_fw_5: 5. Select the waveform that you want to transmit.
label.customized_fw_6: 6. The oscilloscope automatically sends a 2048-byte binary packet over the USB serial connection.
label.customized_fw_7: 7. The packet includes waveform data and metadata such as V/div, timebase, trigger settings, cursors, and measurements.
label.using_viewer_1: The application can receive oscilloscope data in both supported transmission modes.
label.using_viewer_2: After a waveform is received, you can inspect it, measure voltage and time intervals with cursors, and export the result as a PNG image or CSV data.
label.using_viewer_3: Before receiving data, connect the oscilloscope using a USB Type-C cable, select the correct serial port, and click Listen. Keep the application listening while starting the transmission from the oscilloscope.
label.firmware_warning: ⚠ WARNING: Flashing incorrect firmware may brick your device. Ensure the device is in boot mode and the correct firmware file is selected.
label.boot_1: 1. Connect the supplied USB cable to your PC while the oscilloscope is powered off.
label.boot_2: 2. Press and hold the power button. The scope may enter a power-cycling loop — keep the button held down continuously until flashing reaches 100%.
label.firmware_status_ready: Select firmware file and port, then click Update.
label.firmware_confirm: ⚠ Are you sure? This may brick the device. Click Update again to confirm.
label.firmware_complete: Flash complete! You may close this dialog.
